newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares firm, more gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares firm, more gains expected.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 1.02 percent on Tuesday and traders said further gains were on the cards due to persistent demand for the shares of newly privatised companies.

"Shares of newly privatised companies like Lek, Kolinska and Droga seem to have enough potential to keep attracting domestic and foreign investors and to continue pulling the whole market up," one trader said.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 9.36 points to 925.17.
* 12 shares rose and six fell, while six were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 259.7 million tolars from 232.4 million.
* Lek's A issue, which was listed two weeks ago, had the highest turnover and rose 2.48 percent to 16.603 tolars on volume of 10,944 shares for total turnover of 181.7 million tolars.
* Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the top gainers, surging 8.91 percent to 11,432 on volume of 3,133 shares for total turnover of 35.8 million tolars.

* Financial consultancy Dadas was the leading decliner, falling 6.62 percent to 13,342 on volume of 258 shares for total turnover of 3.4 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
